notes.summary: Conditional noninvariant Gauss domination and convexity: scalar-extended annular comparison bounds every finite continuous scalar-curve-positive torus function by a convex Gauss-point restriction. Generic completed-residue-field coefficients are essential; ground-field monomial curves do not suffice. No exact real-PL or classification conclusion is claimed.
notes.detailedSummary: For a split analytic torus with an ordinary open convex tropical domain, assume the explicit annular comparison foundation F1 over every complete analytic extension. For every finite continuous scalar-curve-positive function h, prove h(x) <= h(kappa(tau(x))) and convexity of t -> h(kappa(t)). Domination follows by successively replacing coordinates with independent radius-one Gauss variables and applying singleton-boundary comparison. Convexity uses a monomial curve over H(kappa(t0)); grouped Laurent coefficients retain their full Gauss norms, so its Gauss points project to the multidimensional Gauss section. Two-endpoint annular comparison and continuity give convexity in all directions. This is a complete implication under F1, whose identification with the unavailable exact primary classical definition is unverified. The argument allows noninvariant functions and essential analytic extensions, but supplies neither necessity nor a general smooth-space envelope theorem.
notes.text:
Assume the following precise foundation F1: a scalar-curve-positive function pulls back to a subharmonic function on every smooth strict open annulus over every complete analytic extension; on a closed strict annulus, harmonic comparison with \(A+B\log|u|\) uses the two Gauss endpoints; on the unit-circle affinoid \(|u|=1\), constant comparison uses its singleton Gauss boundary. This is an explicit assumption, not a result granted by the supplied book or its audits. The exact primary definition was not retrieved.

Let \(K\) be complete and nontrivially valued, \(T=(\mathbf G_{m,K}^n)^{\mathrm{an}}\), \(\tau(x)=(\log|Z_i(x)|)_i\), \(\Omega\subset\mathbf R^n\) open convex, and \(U=\tau^{-1}(\Omega)\). Let \(\kappa_K(t)\) be the Gauss point
\[
\left|\sum_m c_mZ^m\right|_{\kappa_K(t)}
=\max_m|c_m|e^{\langle m,t\rangle}.
\]
Weighted Gauss multiplicativity follows because initial forms multiply in a Laurent polynomial ring over the graded residue field, an integral domain. Thus this is a point, with tropical coordinate \(t\). Finite maxima of continuous coefficient norms prove continuity of \(\kappa_K\) in the Laurent-polynomial evaluation topology. Let \(h\) be finite continuous and scalar-curve-positive; in particular, F1 applies after every complete analytic extension. No invariance is imposed.

For \(x\in U\), take \(E=\mathcal H(x)\), with coordinate images \(a_i\in E^\times\), \(|a_i|=e^{t_i}\), \(t=\tau(x)\). The rational \(E\)-point \((a_i)\) projects to \(x\). Choose \(\epsilon>0\) with \(t+se_j\in\Omega\) for all \(j\) and \(|s|<\epsilon\). Enlarge \(E\), if necessary, by a weighted Gauss variable of norm \(e^\epsilon\) and complete its rational-function field; this preserves original norms and makes the surrounding annuli strict. Define \(E_j\) by adjoining independent radius-one Gauss variables \(S_1,\ldots,S_j\) to \(E\) and completing. Let \(x_j\) be the \(K\)-point obtained by substituting \(Z_i=a_iS_i\) for \(i\le j\), and \(Z_i=a_i\) for \(i>j\).

Over \(E_{j-1}\), the smooth open-annulus map
\[
u\longmapsto(a_1S_1,\ldots,a_{j-1}S_{j-1},a_ju,a_{j+1},\ldots,a_n)
\]
lies in \(U_{E_{j-1}}\) for \(e^{-\epsilon}<|u|<e^\epsilon\). Its point \(u=1\) projects to \(x_{j-1}\), and its unit Gauss point projects to \(x_j\). F1 gives \(h(x_{j-1})\le h(x_j)\). The final independent-variable norm is
\[
\left|\sum_m c_m a^mS^m\right|
=\max_m|c_m|e^{\langle m,t\rangle}.
\]
Hence \(x_n=\kappa_K(t)\) and
\[
h(x)\le h(\kappa_K(\tau(x))).
\]

Set \(a_h(t)=h(\kappa_K(t))\), a finite continuous function. To prove its convexity, fix an integer direction \(w\) and a compact segment \(t_0+rw\subset\Omega\), enlarged slightly along the same line. Take \(E=\mathcal H(\kappa_K(t_0))\) and coordinate images \(a_i\). The monomial curve \(u\mapsto(a_i u^{w_i})_i\) has, for \(P=\sum_m c_mZ^m\), the coefficient
\[
B_k=\sum_{\langle m,w\rangle=k}c_ma^m
\]
of \(u^k\). By the defining norm of this completed residue field,
\[
|B_k|=\max_{\langle m,w\rangle=k}|c_m|e^{\langle m,t_0\rangle}.
\]
Consequently its radius-\(e^r\) Gauss point projects to \(\kappa_K(t_0+rw)\), since
\[
|P(\gamma(\eta_{e^r}))|
=\max_m|c_m|e^{\langle m,t_0+rw\rangle}.
\]
For any desired two endpoint radii, enlarge \(E\) by independent weighted Gauss variables at those radii and at two slightly exterior radii, then complete. This is an isometric complete analytic extension and makes both closed and surrounding open annuli strict. F1 compared with the harmonic chord gives
\[
a_h(t_0+((1-\theta)r_0+\theta r_1)w)
\le(1-\theta)a_h(t_0+r_0w)+\theta a_h(t_0+r_1w).
\]
Every rational vector is proportional to an integer vector. Approximate any displacement \(t_1-t_0\) by rational vectors with endpoints still in \(\Omega\); convexity of \(\Omega\) retains their segments. Continuity of \(a_h\) gives the general convex inequality by taking limits.

The scalar coefficients are necessary for this argument. The ground-field diagonal \(u\mapsto(u,u)\) annihilates \(Z_1-Z_2\), whereas its norm at the two-dimensional unit Gauss point is \(1\), in every residue characteristic. Thus an ordinary monomial curve with ground-field coefficients does not realize the multidimensional Gauss section. The completed-residue-field coefficient calculation above repairs precisely that defect. This is an exact algebraic calculation, not a psh-envelope counterexample.

The proof is a conditional mathematical implication, not an exhaustive finite result or an experimental observation. F1's specialization to the intended classical definition remains unverified against a full primary source. Nothing here proves that the exact LFS or semipositive real-PL classes satisfy F1, or proves a branch necessity theorem. Full proof and scope are in P03.1-argument.md and the standalone P03.1-paper.tex. To regenerate the TeX source run python3 make-paper.py; to compile it twice run python3 rerun.py. No supplied or previous local note is used.

notes.summary: Conditional full-family toric computation and scalar compatibility: for bounded open convex tropical domains and tropical usc obstacles with a finite convex minorant, all continuous scalar-psh minorants and all conventional LFS minorants, including noninvariant ones, have envelope p composed with tropicalization. The exact P03 union requires an unproved real-PL bridge; the original sharp classification remains unsolved.
notes.detailedSummary: Using n1 and explicit foundations F2 (unit logarithms harmonic on every required curve after every analytic extension, with local harmonic comparison) and F3 (the conventional max-log LFS class), compute both full noninvariant continuous scalar-curve-positive and full locally LFS envelopes as the finite continuous convex envelope p of the tropical obstacle. Gauss restriction gives the upper bound for every competitor. Supporting affine functions, rational slope approximation with a bounded-domain downward correction, and common-denominator finite maxima give global LFS minorants achieving the lower bound. The same computation over every analytic extension proves exact compatibility of the separately defined full families and commutation of ground-field regularization with pullback in this sector. Only conditionally, if every exact real-PL competitor is finite continuous scalar-curve-positive, the original full union is squeezed to this function. F1-F3 and the PL inclusion were not verified from a full public primary source. Arbitrary obstacles, target relative boundary, sharp normal/unibranch hypotheses and branch/pinching necessity remain unresolved; no CLD-v2 claim is made.
notes.text:
Retain n1's notation and foundation F1, and now assume \(\Omega\) is bounded. Impose the following additional explicit foundations. F2: on every curve required by the intended classical definition, over every complete analytic extension, the logarithm of the absolute value of an analytic unit is harmonic; constants and real linear combinations remain harmonic; harmonic functions obey local boundary comparison defining subharmonicity. If the definition requires singular test curves, F2 includes them; no unproved reduction to smooth tests is used. F3: the exact LFS class in this conditional application has local presentations
\[
h=m^{-1}\max_i(\lambda_i+\log|g_i|),
\qquad m\in\mathbf Z_{>0},\quad\lambda_i\in\mathbf R,
\]
with analytic \(g_i\) having no common zero, including rational-slope monomials and common-denominator finite maxima. A local invertible denominator is absorbed into \(g_i\). These foundations and identification with the original definitions have not been verified from a retrieved primary proof.

Let \(\varphi:\Omega\to\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}\) be usc with a finite convex minorant \(a_0\), put \(f=\varphi\circ\tau\), and define
\[
p=\sup\{a:\Omega\to\mathbf R\text{ finite convex},\ a\le\varphi\}.
\]
The minorant excludes \(-\infty\) values of \(\varphi\), and its codomain excludes \(+\infty\). Thus \(a_0\le p\le\varphi\) is finite; taking suprema of convex inequalities proves convexity. On a compact ball inside \(\Omega\), usc bounds \(\varphi\) above and continuity of finite convex \(a_0\) bounds it below. A convex chord extended from either of two points in the quarter-radius ball at least half the original radius bounds the secant slope by \(2(M-m)/R\). Reversing the points proves local Lipschitz continuity of \(p\). The usual continuity of finite convex \(a_0\) follows by the same chord argument, obtaining a local upper bound from the values at vertices of a surrounding box, and a lower bound by reflection about its center. This uses no common modulus for the original analytic family.

Let \(\mathcal C_{K,f}\) be the entire family of finite continuous scalar-curve-positive minorants. For every \(h\) in this family, n1 proves that \(a_h(t)=h(\kappa_K(t))\) is a finite convex minorant of \(\varphi\), and
\[
h(x)\le a_h(\tau(x))\le p(\tau(x)).
\]
This upper bound covers noninvariant competitors.

For the reverse bound and positivity, every finite convex \(p\) on an open convex set has supporting affine functions: local Lipschitz bounds make its directional derivative finite and sublinear; a dominated linear functional exists by finite-dimensional one-vector-at-a-time sublinear extension; convexity makes this a global support. The supports represent \(p\). On any compact subset, continuity of each support's gap from \(p\) and a finite cover give uniform approximation from below by their finite maxima.

After any complete analytic extension \(E/K\) and any required curve map \(g:C\to U_E\), the coordinate pullbacks \(G_i=Z_i\circ g\) are analytic units. By F2, every supporting affine function pulls back to a real linear combination of the harmonic functions \(\log|G_i|\). A finite maximum of harmonic functions is subharmonic by comparison: domination on the boundary implies domination of each harmonic summand throughout. A locally uniform limit is subharmonic because boundary error \(\epsilon\) permits comparison against the harmonic comparator plus \(\epsilon\), followed by the limit and \(\epsilon\downarrow0\). Therefore \(p\circ\tau\) is finite continuous scalar-curve-positive and below \(f\). The entire continuous scalar-curve-positive family has raw envelope exactly \(p\circ\tau\).

Under F2-F3, every locally LFS function is scalar-curve-positive. Its presentation survives every analytic extension and curve pullback. At a fixed curve point at least one generator is nonzero. Terms whose norms vanish there can be dropped in a small neighborhood since they are strictly below a finite nonzero term; all remaining generators become units on a smaller neighborhood. The function is then a positive multiple of a finite maximum of harmonic functions. Locality proves subharmonicity on the complete test curve. Hence the upper bound applies to the entire noninvariant LFS minorant family \(\mathcal L_{K,f}\).

For its lower bound, fix \(t_0\) and a support
\[
\ell(t)=p(t_0)+\langle b,t-t_0\rangle\le p(t).
\]
Let \(D=\sup_{t\in\Omega}\|t-t_0\|<\infty\). For \(q\in\mathbf Q^n\), define
\[
\ell_q(t)=p(t_0)+\langle q,t-t_0\rangle-D\|q-b\|.
\]
Cauchy-Schwarz gives \(\ell_q\le\ell\le p\le\varphi\) everywhere, while \(\ell_q(t_0)\to p(t_0)\). If \(q=v/m\), the pullback is \(c+m^{-1}\log|Z^v|\), a global LFS minorant by F3. Consequently
\[
\sup\mathcal L_{K,f}=p\circ\tau=\sup\mathcal C_{K,f}.
\]
Boundedness is used in this downward correction; no full LFS equality on an unbounded tropical domain is asserted. A compact exhaustion and finite covers produce finite maxima of these affine minorants approximating \(p\) on each exhaustion set. Cumulative maxima yield a global increasing LFS sequence converging locally uniformly. A common multiple of the slope denominators gives an LFS presentation of each finite maximum. This constructs the lower bound, while n1 gave the upper bound for every competitor; it is not a result about only a selected invariant subfamily.

Over every complete analytic extension \(E/K\), the same argument has the same \(\Omega,\varphi,p\). Since \(\tau_E=\tau_K\circ\pi_{E/K}\), the separately defined full families satisfy
\[
\sup\mathcal L_{E,f\circ\pi_{E/K}}
=(\sup\mathcal L_{K,f})\circ\pi_{E/K}=p\circ\tau_E,
\]
and the same identity holds for \(\mathcal C\). Every raw function computed here is continuous, so
\[
(s_K\circ\pi_{E/K})^*=s_K^*\circ\pi_{E/K}=p\circ\tau_E.
\]
This proves the formal scalar compatibility without assuming scalar projections are open, identifying individual upstairs competitors with descended functions, or confusing ground-field curve tests with scalar stability.

For the original union \(\mathcal E\), the precise remaining bridge is: every semipositive real-PL competitor in its exact definition must be finite continuous scalar-curve-positive after every analytic extension. If that statement and F1-F3 are supplied, then \(\mathcal L\subseteq\mathcal E\subseteq\mathcal C\) squeezes the entire original union envelope to the same function over every field. This conditional implication requires no fiberwise-maximum closure or PL/LFS approximation theorem. The real-PL bridge is not proved here, and no dossier theorem is accepted as its proof.

Even after supplying that bridge, this concerns only tropical obstacles with a finite convex minorant on the displayed bounded convex smooth-torus domains. Arbitrary obstacles, minus-infinity obstacles outside this scope, target relative boundary, normal/geometrically-unibranch singular targets, sharp sufficiency and necessity, and branched/nonsplit-node/codimension-two pinching obstructions remain unresolved. No CLD-v2 claim is made, and continuity of this computed function is not a solution of P03.3. The whole original P03.1 target is not solved.

The complete conditional proof is in P03.1-argument.md and P03.1-paper.tex; its exact application gates are in source-provenance.json and status.json. Run python3 make-paper.py to regenerate the standalone TeX source, then python3 rerun.py to compile twice using the existing installation. Mathematical support is solely n1; artifact existence or compilation is not mathematical support.
